id_and_class.summary: Trialism names a family of theories that recognize three irreducible categories relevant to mind, rather than the one of monism or the two of dualism. John Cottingham reads Descartes as holding three primitive notions (mind, body, and their union, which grounds sensation and passion), while Karl Popper and John Eccles posit three interacting worlds and Roger Penrose links physical, mental, and mathematical domains. The third category does different work in each theory and need not be a third substance.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness Within a Three-Part Structure of Reality

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: No single identity claim. For Cottingham, sensation and passion are irreducibly psychophysical modes of the mind-body union; for Popper and Eccles, consciousness is World 2; for Penrose, it is the mental world that a small part of the physical world generates.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Cottingham’s Descartes treats embodied experience as belonging to the mind-body union, describable neither as pure thought nor as pure extension. Popper and Eccles hold that brain (World 1) and conscious experience (World 2) interact directly and reciprocally, and Penrose has the brain generate the mental world.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Varies by theory: Cartesian trialism treats the union as a primitive notion, Popper and Eccles make World 2 irreducible and interacting, and Penrose has the physical world generate the mental.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: In Popper’s scheme, subjectivity is World 2, and minds create and grasp the objective contents of World 3. In Penrose’s, the mental world comprehends Platonic mathematical truths.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Cottingham locates sensations and passions in the psychophysical union, as irreducible to either intellect or mechanism. The other trialist theories offer no specific account of qualitative feel.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Depends on the version: thought, extension, and their union (Cottingham); physical states, conscious experience, and objective contents of thought (Popper and Eccles); physical, mental, and mathematical or Platonic worlds (Penrose).
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Philosophical analysis of Descartes’s texts and correspondence, introspection, and, for Penrose, mathematical understanding.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Three irreducible categories, related differently in each theory. In Popper’s scheme World 2 mediates between Worlds 1 and 3; in Penrose’s, the three domains form a triangle of instantiation, generation, and comprehension.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (sensation, passion); Mental causation; Knowledge and abstract understanding
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: A third irreducible category whose role varies: psychophysical union for Cottingham, objective knowledge and culture for Popper, mathematical reality for Penrose. Trialism offers no single mechanism for consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: For Popper and Eccles, conscious intentions affect the brain and behavior, and World 3 influences the physical world only through its effects on conscious subjects.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Penrose: a small part of the Platonic world is instantiated in physics, a small part of the physical world generates the mental, and a small part of the mental world explores the Platonic.
core_claims_and_evidence: Descartes distinguished three primitive notions (thought, extension, and the union), and Cottingham reads this as three kinds of property and three kinds of explanation.
Sensations and passions are irreducibly psychophysical, reducible neither to pure intellect nor to mechanism.
Popper divides reality into physical states, conscious experiences, and the objective contents of thought, with consciousness mediating between the other two.
Penrose links physical, mental, and mathematical worlds in a triangle in which each contains a small part of the next.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: textual interpretation of Descartes, metaphysical argument, and reflection on mathematics.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The label covers theories whose third terms do quite different work, so trialism is a family resemblance rather than one doctrine. Cottingham’s reading answers Elisabeth of Bohemia’s challenge about how an immaterial soul moves a body only by naming the union as primitive, and the Popper–Eccles version inherits the usual problems of interactionism.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Whether the third category is a substance, a property, a mode of explanation, or a domain differs from theory to theory, and none of the versions explains why experience is felt.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Each version is coherent within its own frame, but they are not mutually consistent. Cottingham’s trialism concerns properties and explanations rather than a third substance; Penrose does not call his scheme trialism at all.
